## Pull request overview

This pull request aims to organize examples and clean up outdated files by removing test files from the root directory, removing obsolete plugin example files, and adding new comprehensive protocol examples in a `basic/` directory. The intent is to provide better documentation and a clearer learning path for ObjectStack users.

**Changes:**
- Removed 12 outdated test and example files (test-*.ts files, mini-kernel-example.ts, config-loader.ts, etc.)
- Added 6 new protocol example files in examples/basic/
- Added comprehensive documentation (examples/README.md, examples/basic/README.md)
- Updated navigation in todo and crm example READMEs

### Reviewed changes

Copilot reviewed 23 out of 23 changed files in this pull request and generated 9 comments.

The `Role` objects in this example use a `permissions` field that doesn't exist in the actual `Role` type from @objectstack/spec/auth/role.zod.ts.

The actual `Role` schema only has: `name`, `label`, `parent`, `description`

But this example includes a `permissions` object with properties like `manageUsers`, `manageRoles`, etc. These permissions should likely be defined in a separate `PermissionSet` rather than inline in the Role definition.

This will cause TypeScript compilation errors.

The types `RAGPipeline`, `RAGDocument`, `RAGQuery`, and `RAGResult` do not exist in @objectstack/spec. Based on the actual schema definitions in packages/spec/src/ai/rag-pipeline.zod.ts, the correct types should be:
- `RAGPipelineConfig` instead of `RAGPipeline`
- `DocumentChunk` and `DocumentMetadata` instead of `RAGDocument`  
- `RAGQueryRequest` instead of `RAGQuery`
- `RAGQueryResponse` instead of `RAGResult`

This will cause TypeScript compilation errors when building the example.

The type `ETLProcess` does not exist in @objectstack/spec. Based on the actual schema definitions in packages/spec/src/automation/etl.zod.ts, the correct type should be `ETLPipeline` instead of `ETLProcess`.

This will cause TypeScript compilation errors when building the example.
```suggestion
  ETLPipeline,
```

The type `RowLevelSecurity` does not exist in @objectstack/spec. Based on the actual schema definitions in packages/spec/src/permission/rls.zod.ts, the correct type should be `RowLevelSecurityPolicy` instead of `RowLevelSecurity`.

This will cause TypeScript compilation errors when building the example.
```suggestion
  RowLevelSecurityPolicy,
```

The type `ApiDiscoveryResponse` does not exist in @objectstack/spec. Based on the actual schema definitions in packages/spec/src/api/discovery.zod.ts, the correct type should be `DiscoveryResponse` instead of `ApiDiscoveryResponse`.

This will cause TypeScript compilation errors when building the example.

The structure of the `fullDiscoveryResponse` object does not match the actual `DiscoveryResponse` type defined in packages/spec/src/api/discovery.zod.ts. 

The actual schema has: `name`, `version`, `environment`, `routes`, `features`, `locale`

But this example uses: `system`, `endpoints`, `capabilities`, `auth`, `objects`, `features`, `links`

The example appears to be using a completely different structure that doesn't exist in the spec. This will cause type errors and needs to be rewritten to match the actual schema definition.

The `User` objects in this example use fields that don't exist in the actual `User` type from @objectstack/spec/auth/identity.zod.ts.

The actual `User` schema only has: `id`, `email`, `emailVerified`, `name`, `image`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt`

But this example uses: `id`, `email`, `name`, `authProvider`, `emailVerified`, `avatar`, `timezone`, `locale`, `active`, `lastLogin`, `roles`

Fields like `authProvider`, `avatar`, `timezone`, `locale`, `active`, `lastLogin`, and `roles` do not exist in the spec and will cause TypeScript compilation errors.
